label: Aruba Instant On 1830 24G 12p Class4 PoE 2SFP 195W Switch (JL813A)
description: Aruba Instant On 1830 24G 12p Class 4 PoE 2SFP 195W (JL813A) - 24x 1G RJ45 with 802.3at Class 4 PoE on ports 1-12 (195 W budget) plus 2x 1G SFP uplinks.

poe.note: JL813A: 195 W Class 4 PoE across ports 1-12.

notes: Datasheet (https://www.also.com/ec/cms5/media/img/2900/microsites_9/hpe_8/aruba_3/aruba_instant_on_1/product_datasheet/ds_aio_1830switchseries.pdf): "8 RJ-45 autosensing 10/100/1000 ports IEEE 802.3at Class 4 PoE (ports 1-4)" for the JL811A, "(ports 1-12)" for the JL813A and "(ports 1-24)" for the JL815A. The Installation and Getting Started guide prints the same split as a table - "PoE Port Count: Ports 1 - 4" (JL811A), "Ports 1 - 12" (JL813A), "Ports 1-24" (JL815A), with a 65/195/370 W maximum - and the regulatory sheet prints "30W per port, 4 ports, total max. output power 65W" (https://arubanetworking.hpe.com/techdocs/hardware/switches/1830/1830_IGSG.pdf, https://arubanetworking.hpe.com/techdocs/hardware/switches/1830/1830_SH_EN.pdf). WHAT WAS WRONG - the spec named the PoE subset only in the free-text poe note and left every copper port silent, so the engine inferred an 802.3af 15.4 W PSE on all 8/24/48 of them: the data-only sockets powered powered devices, the PoE sockets advertised 15.4 W instead of the Class 4 30 W the sheet prints, and show power inline listed sockets that cannot source a watt. The ports now carry the vendor split: 30 W PoE+ on the PoE ports, an explicit 0 on the data-only ports (0 is the spec's way of saying "this port sources nothing"; a null would be read as silence and re-inferred).
